── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 27, 37, 53, 40 mi
This week: 42 mi over 5 runs.
Feeling: "Anxious about the new date."
Asks: "The race got moved two weeks earlier, to October 18, because of the bridge works. That's three weeks from today. I've only done one 20. Do I still have time for my 22-miler?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: You nailed every session last week, so this is your final big weekend before taper: one dress-rehearsal long run of 20 mi with marathon pace…
Answers: (1) No 22-miler, and you do not need one. The race is two weekends away, so Sunday Oct 4 is the last long run that can actually train you; anything after that is taper and just recovers the legs. (2) Here is the better trade: run 20 mi on Sunday with the last 6 mi at marathon pace (around 8:35/mi). That gives you more race-specific work than a slow 22 would, confirms the pace feels controlled, and still lets you taper cleanly.
Next week:
Mon: rest. Full day off the legs before the Wednesday quality session.
Tue: easy, 6 mi, heart rate under 145, flat route. Loosen up and set up Wednesday.
Wed: quality, 8 mi with 4 mi at marathon pace (8:35/mi) in the middle, 2 mi warm-up and…
Thu: easy, 6 mi, heart rate under 145. Keep it conversational; let Wednesday settle.
Fri: rest. Protect Sunday.
Sat: easy, 4 mi plus 4 x 20 sec strides at the end. Wake the legs up without taxing them.
Sun: long, 20 mi, first 14 mi easy around 9:55/mi, last 6 mi at marathon pace (8:35/mi)…
